core_obligations: Bound the ranks: since X is affine and F is of finite presentation it is generated by c elements, so dim_{kappa(x)}(F_x tensor kappa(x)) is at most c for every x, giving H_p empty for p > c and the inclusion of the disjoint union into F_d (proof lines 7789-7794).

Reduce the converse to a local statement: for a base change F_T flat in dimensions at least d over T and t in T, show that F_T is free of some rank r on an open neighbourhood U of the unique generic point xi of the fibre X_t, so that H_r contains the image of U, which is an open neighbourhood of t (proof lines 7794-7799).
Obtain U from the flat-and-free-at-a-point-of-the-fibre lemma and conclude the equality F_d = disjoint union of the H_p (proof lines 7800-7802).
proof_roadmap: Bound the possible ranks by the number of generators (proof lines 7789-7794).
Turn the statement into a freeness statement at the generic point of the fibre (proof lines 7794-7799).
Quote the flat-and-free local lemma to conclude (proof lines 7800-7802).
difficulty_reason: For a smooth morphism X -> S of affine schemes with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension d and a quasi-coherent module F of finite presentation, the lemma asserts that the functor F_d defined by flatness in dimensions at least d is the disjoint union of the functors H_p of fibrewise freeness of rank p, for p running from 0 to some c (statement lines 7777-7786). The proof first bounds the ranks: since X is affine and F is of finite presentation, F is generated by c elements, so the dimension of F_x tensor kappa(x) never exceeds c and hence H_p is empty for p greater than c, which also shows the inclusion of the disjoint union into F_d (proof lines 7789-7794). The content is then identified precisely: for a base change F_T flat in dimensions at least d over T and a point t of T, one must show that F_T is free of some rank r on an open neighbourhood of the generic point of the fibre X_t, because then H_r contains the image of that neighbourhood, which is an open neighbourhood of t; this existence is quoted from the flat-and-free-at-a-point-of-the-fibre lemma (proof lines 7795-7802). Identifying the two functors through the generic point of the fibre is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
